issue.body:
### Description

This is adapted from here: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/discussions/31127

I understand that `jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint` is not meant for eager regions but the following seems like a bug, perhaps lying with something unrelated to `jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint`. There @yashk2810 mentioned the eager behavior was implemented with `out_shardings`.

The following fails:

```python
import jax
import numpy as np
import jax.numpy as jnp

cpu = jax.devices()[0]
sharding = jax.sharding.SingleDeviceSharding(cpu)

x = jnp.arange(10)  # jax array
y_wsc = jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint(x, sharding)
y_put = jax.device_put(x, sharding)
assert y_wsc.committed == y_put.committed == True  # This fails; y_wsc.committed = False
```

While strangely, this passes:

```python
import jax
import jax.sharding as jshard
import numpy as np
import jax.numpy as jnp

jax.config.update("jax_num_cpu_devices", 2)

num_devices = len(jax.devices())
mesh = jax.make_mesh((num_devices,), ("batch",))
sharding = jshard.NamedSharding(mesh, jshard.PartitionSpec("batch"))

x = jnp.arange(10)  # jax array
y_wsc = jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint(x, sharding)
y_put = jax.device_put(x, sharding)
assert y_wsc.committed == y_put.committed == True  # This passes
```

Also strangely, if I set `x = np.arange(10)`, both cases pass.

issue.title: Update autoparallelism tutorial

issue.body:
I've updated the autoparallelism tutorial (#1067) to remove the deprecated syntax as of JAX 0.7.0. I had some questions about how exactly to update the tutorial in this issue, but I decided to go ahead and do it for what seems to be correct as per JAX for the current state of equinox. The one thing I am not sure about is if `eqx.filter_shard` via `jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint` can really be used as `jax.device_put`. Therefore, in the updated tutorial I only call `eqx.filter_shard` inside the jitted region.

If we wanted to instead apply the sharding in eager regions, then I would recommend we add a `eqx.filter_device_put`. If we do this, it is not necessary to call `eqx.filter_shard` on the inputs of the `train_step` function (just the outputs).

It seemed to me that addressing #1077 would really be the best thing to do. However, from looking through the code it looks like there would be a relatively large refactor of the `eqx.filter_jit` internals to do this; the `_filter_jit_cache` is called before the arguments are preprocessed, but it would have to be the other way around in order to implement what I proposed. I imagine there is a good reason why this is the case too, so I wanted to leave it alone.
